new_issues.title: status/coverage exit 4 (storage) when the production calendar URL setting is unset, though READ_EPILOG puts a missing setting under exit 1
new_issues.why: The new _read helper calls calendar_url(settings), which turns DatabaseNotConfiguredError into TickCalendarError; run_mapped then uses exit_code_for, which maps TickCalendarError to EXIT_STORAGE. The new READ_EPILOG says a setting is preflight (1) and 4 means an unreachable database, so the code contradicts its own help text. The error message naming the missing variable is still printed, so the effect is a misclassified exit code only, the same class as 225-I6.

new_issues.title: No load test covers the coverage read path's bounded tick_trade scan
new_issues.why: True: the slice adds raw_counts over tick_trade, and the only 225 load test (test_225_tick_ingest_nfr.py) covers ingest; the project's python rules ask for a load test on network/environment paths. This is a missing test, not a shown defect; whether the scan is actually slow is the separate UNSURE issue 225-I4.

new_issues.title: _scope's held-day calendar bounds (midnight(d), midnight(d+1)) fall outside the populated span at the calendar's edges, failing status
new_issues.why: Days the pass plans come from session_days, which calls sessions_between(midnight(start), midnight(end)) and so never emits a day whose next midnight passes last_close, nor one whose midnight precedes first_open (the 225 TD7 test asserts the horizon half). So the 'normal case for an ingest caught up to the horizon' cannot happen, and the first-session claim is wrong because session F opens at 22:00 on F-1, before midnight(F). Only an adopted unit outside the calendar could reach it, which ingest itself rejects as session_boundary.

new_issues.title: The degraded tally is appended to the last bucket row, after 'edge unknown'
new_issues.why: _product_lines does lines[-1] += '(degraded N)', so it prints after 'edge unknown N'. That is exactly the layout the slice design specifies ('... edge unknown <n>   (degraded <n>)'), so it is a cosmetic readability preference, not a defect.
